title: A holder frozen past the stale/takeover rule inside an un-opt is protected only by the pre-rename owns() check
evidence: Same advisory-lock limit as every other store mutation (see ISS-LOCKTAKE-005): a holder stalled inside afterRead longer than the stale/takeover rule could lose its lock. recordTenantUnOptOut re-checks ownership immediately before the rename (test: 'a lock taken over mid-operation'), so the stalled writer throws locked and writes nothing, but a thief that is itself mid-write is not covered by anything beyond that check. Not reproduced; recorded for completeness, not fixed here.
fix_direction: Same as ISS-LOCKTAKE-005; no change specific to un-opt.

title: PUT /calendar/join-rules writes the caller's earlier snapshot of the opt-out state back: a PUT in flight erases an opt-out made by another process after the PUT's load, and the meeting becomes joinable
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/router.ts PUT (load, then deps.save({ruleSet, state: existing.state})); packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-store.ts saveJoinRules (full replace, lock only around the write)
evidence: Executed by checker on ecf16b7 with a temporary probe, real store, real second node process: seed rules allow x.com, state empty; PUT-shaped sequence existing=loadJoinRules; a separate node process calls recordTenantOptOut(cal1) (file then lists ['cal1']); saveJoinRules(ruleSet, existing.state) -> optedOutEventIds [] and evaluateJoinRules(cal1) = 'join'. Not reachable inside the one API host process today (the router chains PUT, approve, opt-out and un-opt per tenant, and the host pid lock allows one host), so it needs a second writer process; same precondition that made ISS-UNOPT-001 medium. This unit leaves PUT unchanged (not worse; un-opt is now locked) but the manifest records it only as a NOT-guaranteed note, with no ledger row.
fix_direction: Make PUT a locked read-modify-write that keeps the CURRENT stored state (replace ruleSet only, state taken under the lock), e.g. saveRuleSet(stateDir, tenant, ruleSet) in the store, or the planned ETag compare-and-set done inside the lock; add a real-process test that opts out between the PUT's load and its write.
